Used cars don't have to be scary, and can be a heck of a lot cheaper to drive than new ones if you A: use your brain, and B: do a little homework.

I like to break a car's life into thirds. Using a Honda Accord as an example, they'll generally run 300k highway miles, and last 25-30 years before all the rubber parts go bad.

The first third is 0-100k and 8 years. By the end of this, the car will depreciate 2/3 in price ($24k to $8k) while it's only 1/3 used up. The car is at its most reliable and warranted, and costs roughly $167/mo in depreciation.

The second third is 100-200k, and 8-16 years. By the end of this, the car will depreciate from $8k to $2k (roughly $63/mo). The car is still very reliable during this time.

The last third is 200+ miles and 16+ years. At this point depreciation is pretty much meaningless, and you drive it until something major blows up.

I try to drive cars in the second category, and put $100/mo away to save up for the next one when I've used up my favorite third of the car.
